speaker: narrator
text: What if Earth flew through a *comet's tail* today?

speaker: narrator
text: Monday. A new comet lights up the *evening sky*.

speaker: narrator
text: Astronomers call it Comet *Vela*. It's beautiful.

speaker: narrator
text: Then the news finds one small *detail*.

speaker: narrator
text: Phones buzz. Every phone. All at *once*.

speaker: narrator
text: The tail contains a poison gas. *Cyanogen*.

speaker: narrator
text: And on Friday night, Earth passes *through it*.

speaker: boss
text: Everybody stay calm! *I* am calm!

speaker: narrator
text: Mayor Doyle is wearing a *gas mask*.

speaker: boss
text: It's my *lucky* gas mask.

speaker: hero
text: Bit, how bad is this? *Honestly*.

speaker: bit
text: Honestly? Earth already did this. In *1910*.

speaker: bit
text: On May nineteenth, 1910, we flew through Halley's *tail*.

speaker: bit
text: Scientists found cyanogen in that tail *too*.

speaker: hero
text: And? What *happened*?

speaker: bit
text: The planet *panicked*.

speaker: hero
text: The whole *planet*?

speaker: narrator
text: At the door, Grandpa Ezra holds a dusty *box*.

speaker: scientist
text: My grandpa bought these in 1910.

speaker: narrator
text: The label says: *comet pills*.

speaker: narrator
text: Real history. And it's about to *repeat*.

speaker: narrator
text: Tuesday. Bit opens the old 1910 *newspapers*.

speaker: bit
text: A famous French astronomer, Camille *Flammarion*, warned...

speaker: bit
text: ...the gas could snuff out *all life*.

speaker: bit
text: He didn't even say it was *likely*.

speaker: bit
text: Too late. People bought *anti-comet pills*.

speaker: hero
text: Comet *umbrellas*?

speaker: bit
text: Very popular. Zero *stars*.

speaker: bit
text: Some people papered over their *keyholes*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay's mom tapes the *keyhole*. Just in case.

speaker: narrator
text: Now it's 2026. And the town chat *explodes*.

speaker: narrator
text: Somebody already sells them *online*.

speaker: narrator
text: Forty-nine left. *Thirty*. *Twelve*.

speaker: boss
text: I bought two hundred. For the *town*.

speaker: friend
text: Two hundred? Mayor, they're ninety-nine *dollars*!

speaker: bit
text: And nobody tested a single *pill*.

speaker: boss
text: Each. Yes. *Safety first*.

speaker: narrator
text: Milo opens his piggy bank. Ten *dollars*.

speaker: kid
text: Is it enough for *one pill*?

speaker: narrator
text: Jay looks at Bit. Bit looks at the *website*.

speaker: bit
text: Jay. Something about this shop is *wrong*.

speaker: narrator
text: Wednesday. Bit traces the StarSafe *Shop*.

speaker: bit
text: The website was made... on *Monday*.

speaker: hero
text: One hour after the comet *news*.

speaker: narrator
text: Nia orders one pill. For *science*.

speaker: narrator
text: It arrives the next morning in a tiny *envelope*.

speaker: narrator
text: Bit scans it. Jay and Nia *lean in*.

speaker: bit
text: Ingredients: sugar. Food coloring. And... more *sugar*.

speaker: friend
text: A ninety-nine dollar *candy*.

speaker: hero
text: And the gas? Is the gas *real*?

speaker: narrator
text: Grandpa Ezra spreads out his old *star charts*.

speaker: scientist
text: A comet tail is huge. But *thin*.

speaker: scientist
text: Flammarion said it: far sparser than a *cloud*.

speaker: bit
text: Translation: the scary gas is basically *nothing*.

speaker: hero
text: Then we tell everyone. *Tonight*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay posts a video. Sugar, sugar, *sugar*.

speaker: narrator
text: Three likes. One is his *mom*.

speaker: narrator
text: And the shop posts a new *offer*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mayor Doyle buys *the first one*.

speaker: narrator
text: Thursday. Main Street looks like a *movie*.

speaker: narrator
text: Gas masks. Umbrellas. Tape on every *keyhole*.

speaker: boss
text: Citizens! Pills at noon. Umbrellas at *one*!

speaker: friend
text: Mayor, it's a scam. Bit *tested* the pills.

speaker: boss
text: A robot told you? On the *internet*?

speaker: bit
text: Excuse me. I am a *very* serious robot.

speaker: narrator
text: Bit's screen shows a smiley face. Not *helping*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then Grandpa Ezra steps onto the *bench*.

speaker: scientist
text: In 1910, everyone was scared like you. *Everyone*.

speaker: scientist
text: And Earth flew through that tail. And *nothing* happened.

speaker: scientist
text: The only thing people lost was *money*.

speaker: narrator
text: The crowd laughs. One mask comes *off*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then *ten*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mayor Doyle keeps his on. *Just in case*.

speaker: narrator
text: That night the shop page shows: *closed*.

speaker: friend
text: They ran. With everyone's *money*.

speaker: bit
text: Not everyone's. I kept the *receipts*.

speaker: narrator
text: But Grandpa Ezra isn't *smiling*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay finds Ezra on the porch, looking *up*.

speaker: hero
text: Grandpa, the comet is harmless. Why so *sad*?

speaker: scientist
text: Because I've never actually *seen* one.

speaker: narrator
text: He opens a photo. A boy on a *roof*.

speaker: scientist
text: My grandpa saw Halley's Comet in *1910*.

speaker: scientist
text: He said: it's back in 1986. Watch for *me*.

speaker: narrator
text: In 1986, Ezra was working nights. Clouds. *Missed it*.

speaker: bit
text: Halley comes back in *2061*. July twenty-eighth.

speaker: scientist
text: I'll be a hundred and twelve. I'm not *waiting*.

speaker: bit
text: Fun fact. Mark Twain was born with Halley's *Comet*.

speaker: bit
text: He said he'd leave with it. He *did*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit. That is the *opposite* of fun.

speaker: scientist
text: Ha! I like him. *This* comet is my chance.

speaker: narrator
text: Friday night. Biggest show of the *century*.

speaker: narrator
text: Jay promises. Front row. The best *roof* in town.

speaker: narrator
text: Then Bit checks the *weather*.

speaker: bit
text: Friday night: clouds. A hundred *percent*.

speaker: bit
text: This happened in 1910 too. In *Brooklyn*.

speaker: bit
text: A lady threw a comet party for thirteen *guests*.

speaker: bit
text: Telescope on the roof. And then? *Clouds*.

speaker: friend
text: So we need to get *above* the clouds.

speaker: hero
text: A plane? A *mountain*?

speaker: narrator
text: Milo raises his hand. Shy. *Hopeful*.

speaker: kid
text: Bit can *fly*. A little.

speaker: narrator
text: Everyone turns to *Bit*.

speaker: bit
text: I float. Three feet. Above a *sofa*.

speaker: hero
text: The clouds start at six thousand *feet*.

speaker: narrator
text: So they build *a balloon*.

speaker: narrator
text: Party balloons. Fifty-two of them. All *helium*.

speaker: narrator
text: Bit gets a camera. A *live stream*.

speaker: narrator
text: Grandpa Ezra gets a tablet. And the *roof*.

speaker: narrator
text: Friday, eleven p.m. One hour until *the tail*.

speaker: bit
text: If my battery hits zero up there... I *fall*.

speaker: hero
text: Then we'll *catch* you. Go!

speaker: narrator
text: Bit lets go of Jay's hand. And *rises*.

speaker: narrator
text: Two thousand feet. The town is a little *map*.

speaker: bit
text: This is *higher* than the sofa.

speaker: narrator
text: Four thousand feet. Cold. The camera *fogs*.

speaker: narrator
text: On the roof, the tablet shows *gray*.

speaker: narrator
text: Inside the cloud, Bit sees *nothing*.

speaker: narrator
text: Battery: thirty *percent*.

speaker: bit
text: Hello, cloud. You are very *wet*.

speaker: hero
text: Bit, come back! It's not *worth* it!

speaker: narrator
text: Ezra grips the tablet. *Please*.

speaker: bit
text: Ezra waited forty years. I can wait *one cloud*.

speaker: narrator
text: Five thousand. Five thousand five *hundred*.

speaker: narrator
text: A balloon *pops*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then *two more*.

speaker: narrator
text: Bit starts to *sink*.

speaker: friend
text: Come on, Bit. Come *on*.

speaker: narrator
text: Milo grabs Jay's phone. Types *fast*.

speaker: kid
text: Bit! Drop the *camera case*! It's heavy!

speaker: narrator
text: Bit drops it. Bit *rises*.

speaker: narrator
text: Six thousand feet. Battery: nine *percent*.

speaker: narrator
text: Eleven fifty-nine. Then the cloud *opens*.

speaker: narrator
text: And the signal *dies*.

speaker: narrator
text: The roof is silent. Ezra holds the *tablet*.

speaker: narrator
text: Three seconds. *Four*.

speaker: narrator
text: Then the screen *lights up*.

speaker: narrator
text: Above the clouds: Comet Vela. Huge. *Glowing*.

speaker: narrator
text: Grandpa Ezra doesn't say a *word*.

speaker: scientist
text: Grandpa... I'm *watching* it.

speaker: scientist
text: It's more beautiful than Grandpa *said*.

speaker: narrator
text: Midnight. Earth slides into the *tail*.

speaker: narrator
text: The whole town *holds its breath*.

speaker: narrator
text: And nothing happens. *Exactly* like 1910.

speaker: narrator
text: Battery: two percent. Bit *drifts down*.

speaker: narrator
text: Right into Milo's *arms*.

speaker: bit
text: Told you. Very *serious* robot.

speaker: narrator
text: Ezra hugs Bit. Then Jay. Then the *mayor*.

speaker: narrator
text: Mayor Doyle finally takes off the *mask*.

speaker: narrator
text: Under it, he's wearing *another* one.

speaker: narrator
text: In 1910, everyone survived the tail. Even pill *buyers*.

speaker: narrator
text: Somewhere, a sugar pill rolls under a *sofa*.

speaker: kid
text: Halley comes back in 2061. I'll be *forty-four*.

speaker: kid
text: I'll watch it. For *Grandpa*.

speaker: narrator
text: Follow for a new What if every day.
